aliases: hot-forged experimental steel prior to rolling

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The tested steel was fabricated via VIM (vacuum induction melting) prior to homogenization/forging.
The steel ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h.
Hot forged to a thickness of 40 mm (forging temperature not reported).
Air cooled to room temperature after hot forging.

structures.overall_structure: No obvious lamellar structure before rolling. The microstructure is mainly composed of coarse δ-ferrite and M/A (martensite/austenite) constituents; δ-ferrite predominates, with martensite and austenite coexisting in the gaps of δ-ferrite. The large-sized grains are δ-ferrite and most austenite transformed into martensite after hot forging.

phases_present.morphology: coarse, large-sized grains; predominant phase; needle/plate-like features; no obvious lamellar banding
phases_present.grain_size: coarse (>50 μm; reported for the alloy's stable coarse δ-ferrite at room temperature)

phases_present.morphology: M/A (martensite/austenite) constituents coexisting in the gaps of δ-ferrite; most austenite transformed into martensite after hot forging
M/A (martensite/austenite) constituents coexisting with martensite in the gaps of δ-ferrite

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac SEM equipped with Oxford Aztec EBSD detector; RD-ND plane; etched with 5 vol% HNO3-ethanol solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the microstructure of the hot-forged steel before rolling (control group)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Coarse grains labelled Martensite/Austenite in the upper region and δ-Ferrite below, with needle/plate-like features and no obvious lamellar banding (Fig. 3a, 25 µm scale bar).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-F200 (CF-HR) TEM; specimens ground to 80 µm, punched into 3 mm discs, twin-jet electropolished with 5 vol% HClO4 acetic acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: High-resolution observation of the hot-forged (pre-rolling) microstructure
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 3b (1 µm scale bar) shows dark polygonal grains with internal dislocation lines, no lamellae or carbides visible; Fig. 3c (500 nm) shows banded/needle contrast labelled Martensite/Austenite (upper) and δ-Ferrite (lower).

computational_details.simulation_method: equilibrium thermodynamic calculation of phase diagram and phase composition vs temperature (alloy-level; applies to the tested steel of which this sample is a processing state)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Tested steel composition (C 0.35, Si 0.26, Mn 1.47, Al 4.50, Cr 0.26, Mo 0.28, Ni 1.47, Fe Bal, wt.%)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated carbide stability temperature range (≤750 °C) is consistent with observed carbide presence at low rolling temperature (Fig. 6a).

unmapped_findings: The hot-forged 'before rolling' steel is the control group / parent state for the four rolled conditions R650, R750, R850 and R950; no tensile or Charpy impact property values are reported for this pre-rolling state (all mechanical data in Table 4/Fig. 5 belong to the rolled samples).

In the before-rolling state δ-ferrite predominates as large-sized grains; martensite and austenite coexist in the gaps of δ-ferrite, indicating that most austenite transformed into martensite after hot forging (b0045).
The studied steel was fabricated via VIM (vacuum induction melting), the ingot being homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h, hot forged to 40 mm and air cooled (b0015).
